name: Nora Ray
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember moving with every possession in a flimsy bag.” Friday often includes a stop at the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, where Nora checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I wrote my address on the picture side because the picture looks more like home than my address does.
appearance: Nora has a round face with a pronounced chin. Look for black hair twisted into a small knot. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a faded indigo overshirt with a thin silver ring worn on a cord. In conversation Nora touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word.
personality: Nora always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Nora is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
agenda: To get the home address on the preferred side of the picture.
family: Bailey Solis is Nora’s stepsibling. Nora puts the kettle on. Bailey chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *A scar at the salon*, Bailey says, “I can retouch it away. I offered a print with no edits so the client could make the first choice.”
connections: Ida Henry. They compare how little room a parcel needs to carry the idea of home.
